stem: Which year was the ‘Hindustan Republican Association’ set up –
expl: In October, 1924, Sachindranath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil and others founded the revolutionary organisation ‘Hindustan Republican Association’ at Kanpur. On 9 August, 1925, this organisation looted the government treasury by carrying out a dacoity on the “8 Down Saharanpur–Lucknow Passenger Train” at a place called Kakori on the Lucknow–Saharanpur Division of the Northern Railway. This incident became famous as the Kakori Case (present name—Kakori Train Action). In this case, 43 revolutionaries were arrested, including Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri, who were hanged, while Chandrashekhar Azad escaped.

stem: One of the founder leaders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army was-
expl: After the Kakori Case (Kakori Train Action), due to the repression launched by the police, the Hindustan Republican Association (H.R.A.) suffered a severe setback. However, later, Bijoy/Vijay Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, Jaidev Kapoor, Bhagat Singh, Bhagwati Charan Vohra and Sukhdev began the work of reorganising the H.R.A. under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad. In September, 1928, a meeting was held at the Feroz Shah Kotla Ground (Delhi) under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, in which the name of the H.R.A. was changed to ‘Hindustan Socialist Republican Association’ (H.S.R.A.).

stem: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed on –
expl: Two members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (H.S.R.A.), Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April, 1929. Both were arrested and tried under the Central Assembly Bomb Case. Later, other members of the H.S.R.A. were also arrested, and the revolutionaries were tried under the Lahore Conspiracy Case. In 1930, the judgment in the Lahore Conspiracy Case was delivered, in which Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were sentenced to death. On 23 March, 1931, all three were hanged. The news of their execution plunged the entire country into deep mourning.

stem: The Chittagong Armoury Raid had been planned by :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was organized by the revolutionary Surya Sen, popularly known as “Master Da”. Surya Sen founded the Indian Republican Army (I.R.A.) in Bengal. Its prominent members included Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty, Lokinath, Pritilata Waddedar, Ganesh Ghosh, Kalpana Dutt, and Anand Gupta. On 18 April, 1930, Surya Sen declared war against the British. Under his leadership, I.R.A. members attacked the Chittagong armoury and seized weapons. On 22 May, 1930, a clash took place between the I.R.A. members and the army, in which 80 soldiers and 12 revolutionaries were killed. Surya Sen was arrested on 16 February, 1933. He was tried and was hanged on 12 January, 1934.
